name: IMPROVE
aliases: Investigation to Minimize Prolapse Recurrence Of the Vagina using Estrogen
question: Does perioperative vaginal conjugated estrogen reduce failure after native-tissue vaginal apical prolapse repair compared with placebo?

design.blinding: participants, surgeons, and outcome assessors masked
design.population: Postmenopausal women aged at least 48 years with bothersome apical and/or anterior prolapse at least to the hymen planning native-tissue transvaginal apical repair.
design.locator: JAMA full text, Methods/Study Population and Randomization; Results/Study Population, Figure 2

verdictNote: The prespecified superiority endpoint was not met; its confidence interval remains wide.
takeaway: Perioperative vaginal conjugated estrogen cream did not improve 12-month composite surgical success versus placebo after native-tissue vaginal apical repair; model-estimated failure was 19% versus 9% (adjusted HR 1.97, 95% CI 0.92–4.22).

reports.label: Twelve-month randomized report
reports.citation: Rahn DD, Richter HE, Sung VW, et al. Perioperative Vaginal Estrogen as Adjunct to Native Tissue Vaginal Apical Prolapse Repair: A Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA.* 2023;330(7):615-625. doi:10.1001/jama.2023.12317
reports.followUp: 12 months after surgery; 186/199 randomized participants underwent surgery and had postoperative assessment
reports.followUpLocator: JAMA full text, Results/Study Population and Primary Outcome, Figure 2

results.measure: Model-estimated 12-month failure incidence; adjusted hazard ratio for estrogen versus placebo
results.note: Modified intention-to-treat analysis included 93 operated participants per arm; percentages are interval-censored model estimates, not 20/93 and 10/93. Failure comprised specified anatomic descent, bothersome bulge, or retreatment. Two-sided superiority alpha was 0.05.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Methods/Outcomes and Results/Primary Outcome, Figure 3

results.measure: Much or very much better on PGI-I at 12 months
results.note: Observed respondents; percentages recalculated from published numerators and denominators.

results.measure: Mean rating at surgery on a 1-to-5 scale; mean difference in points
results.note: Masked surgeons rated tissue into which apical fixation sutures were placed.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Table 2 and Results/Secondary Outcomes

results.measure: Adjusted mean symptom score at 12 months among those bothered at baseline; mean difference in points
results.note: Baseline-bothersome subgroup (n=109); adjusted effect is the difference in change, not subtraction of endpoint means. Questionnaire was study-designed and not validated.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Table 3 and Results/Secondary Outcomes

harms.label: At least one postoperative urinary tract infection
harms.locator: JAMA full text, Table 2 and Results/Adverse Events
harms.note: Through 12 months; P=0.38. Total UTI episodes were 20 versus 33.

harms.label: Granulation tissue after postoperative month 6
harms.note: P=0.048; no repeat operation for granulation tissue.

harms.label: Suture exposure after postoperative month 6
harms.note: Table 2 denominators used; article prose instead says 15/97 for the placebo arm. No repeat operation for suture exposure.

delivery.label: Cream schedule
delivery.value: Conjugated estrogen 0.625 mg/g, 1 g intravaginally nightly for 2 weeks, then twice weekly to complete at least 5 total preoperative weeks; resumed at discharge and continued twice weekly for 12 postoperative months; placebo matched.

delivery.label: Operations performed
delivery.locator: JAMA full text, Results/Study Population and Table 2
delivery.note: Surgeon selected the apical route; suspension was standardized with permanent and delayed absorbable monofilament sutures, with vaginal hysterectomy if the uterus remained.

delivery.label: Concomitant procedures

values.exp: hysterectomy 76/93; anterior repair 82/93; posterior repair 61/93; midurethral sling 53/93
values.ctl: hysterectomy 79/93; anterior repair 73/93; posterior repair 59/93; midurethral sling 53/93

delivery.note: Procedures could overlap within a participant.

delivery.label: Cream adherence
delivery.note: At least 50% of expected cream use before surgery and for 12 months after surgery by participant diary.

reports.label: Three-year follow-up
reports.citation: Rahn DD, Richter HE, Sung VW, et al. Three-year outcomes of a randomized clinical trial of perioperative vaginal estrogen as adjunct to native tissue vaginal apical prolapse repair. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2024;231(2):263.e1-263.e10. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2024.04.042
reports.followUp: 36 months after surgery; 164/186 operated participants provided follow-up data

results.measure: Model-estimated failure through 36 months; adjusted hazard ratio for estrogen versus placebo
results.note: Prespecified extended follow-up analysis; the abstract reports 164/186 operated participants with 36-month data. Assigned cream ended after 12 months.

results.measure: Much or very much better on PGI-I at 36 months
results.note: Observed respondents; 51 of 55 participants classified as surgical failures reported this degree of improvement.

delivery.label: Post-protocol vaginal estrogen use at 36 months
delivery.note: Among 160 respondents reporting use; after month 12, vaginal estrogen could be used for atrophy symptoms regardless of original assignment.

relations.note: Used OPTIMAL's uterosacral and sacrospinous suspension framework and a similar composite failure definition.
